title: Biomes and World Climate Regions: The Great Pattern of Life Zones

questions.question: Which biome is characterised by four canopy storeys, latosol soils, and the highest biodiversity on Earth?
questions.rationale: The equatorial rainforest (Koppen Af) receives 2000+ mm year-round, develops heavily leached latosols, and stacks life into multiple canopies — the Congo, Amazon, and Indonesia shelter the richest biodiversity.

questions.question: In the Koppen classification, the code BWh stands for:
questions.rationale: B marks dry climates, W the desert (versus S for steppe), and h the hot variant — BWh is the hot desert of the Sahara, Thar, and Atacama type; adding k instead gives the cold desert (BWk).

questions.question: The Mediterranean climate's signature vegetation of thick, small, waxy leaves is called:
questions.rationale: Dry summers with wet winters select for hard, small, evergreen, fire-resistant leaves — the maquis of the Mediterranean, chaparral of California, and matorral of Chile: one climate recipe, three names.

questions.question: Which soil-and-biome pairing is correct?
questions.rationale: The cold, coniferous taiga leaches minerals into pale ash-grey podzols. Chernozem-type black earths belong to the temperate grasslands, laterite/red soils to the seasonally wet tropics, and tundra supports only thin gley soils over permafrost.

questions.question: The Atacama and Namib deserts are coastal deserts primarily because of:
options: Cold ocean currents and upwelling suppressing rainfall
Their great distance from the sea
questions.rationale: Cold currents (Humboldt, Benguela) chill the air above them; the stable, inversion-capped air rarely rains — producing Earth's driest strips right beside the ocean, often fog-fed rather than rain-fed.

questions.question: Ascending an equatorial mountain reproduces the full sequence of latitudinal zones. This is called:
questions.rationale: Altitude mimics latitude: the Andes climb from tierra caliente through templada and fria to paramo and permanent snow — the whole poleward journey compressed into kilometres.

questions.question: Which biome supports the great herd migrations of the Serengeti?
questions.rationale: Savannas — wet season grass flushes traded against dry-season fires — sustain wildebeest, zebra, and antelope migrations tracking the rain belt, along with fire-adapted acacia and baobab.

questions.question: The largest land biome on Earth is:
questions.rationale: The spruce-pine-fir belt of Siberia, Canada, and Fennoscandia — the taiga — covers more continuous land than any other forest or biome, a store of timber and carbon on thin podzolic soils.

questions.question: Permafrost is the defining condition of which biome?
questions.rationale: Tundra (Koppen ET) locks its subsoil permanently frozen; only a shallow active layer thaws each summer, supporting lichens, mosses, and cushion plants — and thawing permafrost now destabilises everything built on it.

questions.question: By latitude alone the Thar region should be desert-like, yet Rajasthan's eastern fringe turns green every summer. The reason is:
options: The monsoon's seasonal wind reversal pushing moisture inland
A warm current off the coast
questions.rationale: The monsoon overrides the general subtropical-high dryness of the latitude, driving moist summer winds deep inland — vegetation grades from thorn forest to savanna-like grassland where pure latitude would predict sand.
